subject: Literature
title: Virgil's Aeneid and Imperial Poetry
description: One-minute skill: Virgil's Aeneid and Imperial Poetry.

hook.text: Virgil spent eleven years writing Rome's national epic, then begged on his deathbed for it to be destroyed.

buildup.text: The Aeneid tells how the Trojan hero Aeneas sailed to Italy and founded the civilization that became Rome.

discovery.text: Augustus commissioned the poem to legitimize his rule by linking it to a divine mythological ancestry.

twist.text: Augustus ignored Virgil's dying wish, ordered the poem published, and it became the foundation of Latin education.

climax.text: The Aeneid showed that poetry could serve as both supreme art and political propaganda simultaneously.

punchline.text: The poem he wanted burned became Rome's sacred text.

quiz.question: What dual role did the Aeneid serve?
options: It was both a love story and a comedy
It was both supreme art and political propaganda
It was both a history textbook and a religious manual
